independently_confirmed_boundaries: Rejected ignored/altered lifecycle writes roll back public transactions, while the new in-transaction APIs do not commit or roll back caller-owned work.
Native execution cannot commit against TEMP lifecycle shadows or accept a terminal write whose trigger invalidated a previously accepted lifecycle receipt.
Native model-lineage preparation is read-only; short publication does not rehash model/manifests and rejects changed inputs, scope, or attempt. Parent-fsync failure is not acknowledged.
Effect guards require an exact explicit lease, retain uncertain ownership, and classify release failures as HOLD even after an ordinary body exception.
Prepared/committed file receipts are bounded, create-only, exact-reference/hash checked, read-only on validation, and reject the tested mixed-snapshot publication race.
Execution catalog publication and observation validate bounded immutable routing metadata; missing, malformed, redirected, or unreadable declarations cannot silently grant native authority.

limitations: The lineage short-publication mechanism supports regular-file artifacts; directory artifacts are explicitly unsupported there. The legacy finalizer directory compatibility control still passes.
Execution-catalog metadata is routing information, not a capability or permission to mutate a task.
A confirmed file-effect receipt alone is not proof of a SQLite commit. The coordinator must verify current attempt/lifecycle authority and commit ordering.

No global filesystem/SQLite atomic snapshot, arbitrary hostile-writer protection, external worker output isolation, complete native consumer coverage, or restart liveness is established by this bounded run.
No actual training, provider delivery, research quality, statistical significance, or research-efficiency improvement is claimed.
